prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact REST API reference table: readers find an endpoint, then check its method, auth requirement, rate limit, and description.","reading":"Rows are read endpoint-first; the path is the row key, Method/Auth/Rate limit are quick qualifiers scanned across rows, and Description is read last as prose.","groups":["Method, Auth, Rate limit: compact request constraints that belong together and are compared across rows","Endpoint: standalone row identifier and primary scan target","Description: free prose, secondary to route identification"],"keep_intact":["full endpoint path and path parameters such as {jobId}","HTTP methods GET, POST, DELETE","auth values Bearer and Admin","rate-limit tokens such as 600/min"],"may_wrap":["Description text","header labels such as Rate limit and Description","endpoint path only as a deliberate last resort when avoiding horizontal scroll"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[282,76,67,89,180],"idea":"Identifier-first scrolling layout: keep the endpoint and all short metadata unbroken, let Description wrap, and accept horizontal scroll."},{"name":"B","widths":[190,76,67,78,140],"idea":"Balanced partial-scroll compromise: keep Method/Auth/Rate intact, let only Endpoint and Description wrap, and reduce scrolling enough to show the first three columns at 360px."},{"name":"C","widths":[90,76,67,78,48],"idea":"No-scroll metadata squeeze: fit 359px and preserve Method/Auth/Rate values, accepting a heavily split endpoint and a very narrow wrapped Description."}]}
